{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows positive sentiment (e.g., >0.00) and model overestimates prices, especially after recent spikes.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude when true outcomes show mean reversion toward lower levels after sustained high prices.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (e.g., 0.00), to avoid underestimating downward pressure.",
    "Apply a lag correction: if true outcome is significantly lower than forecast, adjust next period’s forecast downward by 5–10% to account for delayed market reaction.",
    "Cap forecast growth after a spike: if model forecasts a sharp upward move following a spike, reduce the slope of the forecast curve to avoid overshoot.",
    "When sentiment history includes a 0.33 or higher positive sentiment, increase forecast volatility to reflect heightened market anticipation.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction to future forecasts by 3–5% per day."
  ]
}
